title: Patch: clicking another attacker while one is picked switches the attack to it
thread:
**Issue #1791 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #1791: Patch: clicking another attacker while one is picked switches the attack to it
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
A player picks one of their units to attack, changes their mind, and clicks a different unit that can also attack. Today nothing happens. They have to click the first unit again to put it down, then click the second. The second unit already looks clickable, so this feels broken. Once built, that second click picks up the new attacker, the way dragging it already does.

## Why
- `apps/web/src/game/actions.ts:776-780` (`highlightFor`, attacking stage) keeps every other legal attacker lit, with the comment "Any other unit the engine listed as an attacker stays clickable, so the player can switch."
- `onClickTarget`'s `unit`/`backrow` case (`actions.ts:957-966`) breaks that promise. While attacking, it looks for the click only among the picked attacker's own targets. A click on another attacker matches nothing and returns `{ interaction }` unchanged: no switch, no notice.
- The only test, "leaves the other attackers live while an attack is in flight" (`actions.test.ts:946-961`), checks the highlight and never clicks.
- Dragging already switches: `planAttack` (`apps/web/src/game/drag/model.ts:123-142`) lifts any legal attacker even while another is picked, so click and drag disagree.

## Proposal
In the attacking branch of `onClickTarget`, when the attack-target lookup finds nothing, use the path an idle click on a unit already takes (`attacksBy(legal, target.instanceId)`, `actions.ts:984-994`): if the clicked unit has attacks, return `{ interaction: { stage: "attacking", attackerId: target.instanceId, candidates } }`. R1200's rule still applies: a single random-target attack is sent at once.
- A click on a unit that is a target of the picked attacker still attacks it, as today.
- `Game.handleClick` (`Game.tsx:488-503`) already plays the pick-up sound when `attackerId` changes, so nothing else needs to change.
- Legality still comes only from `legalActions` (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

## Where it lands
- `apps/web/src/game/actions.ts` (`onClickTarget`)
- `apps/web/src/game/actions.test.ts`
- No spec change: this is client input only (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With legal attacks for `u1` and `u2`, clicking `u1` then `u2` gives `{ stage: "attacking", attackerId: "u2" }` and no action.
- [ ] Clicking a unit that is a legal target of the picked attacker still returns that attack.
- [ ] Clicking the picked attacker again still drops it.
- [ ] Clicking a unit with no legal attack while attacking leaves the interaction unchanged.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/game/actions.test.ts`, `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and eslint pass.

## Size and risks
Extra small: a few lines in one function and four unit tests. One risk: a unit that is both a target of the picked attacker and an attacker itself. The target reading must win, and the second criterion pins that.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-7` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40115890929)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Right now, if an attack is in flight (stage `"attacking"`) and the player clicks a different unit that `legal` lists as an attacker, nothing happens. After this change, that click switches the attack to the new unit: `{ stage: "attacking", attackerId: <new>, candidates: <its attacks> }`. If R1200 applies (the unit's only attack is a random-target one), the attack is sent at once instead. Four things stay as they are:
- A click on a target of the picked attacker still sends that attack, and the target reading wins over the switch.
- A second click on the picked attacker still drops it.
- A click on a unit with no legal attack leaves the interaction unchanged.
- Legality still comes only from `legal` (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

## Files to touch

| Path | Kind | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/game/actions.ts` | change | New private helper `startAttack`; the `"unit"`/`"backrow"` case of `onClickTarget` uses it in both the attacking branch and the idle path |
| `apps/web/src/game/actions.test.ts` | change | Five new `it(...)`s at the end of `describe("the attack flow", …)` |

Do not touch:
- `apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx`: `handleClick` already plays the pick-up sound when a new attacking interaction comes back.
- `apps/web/src/game/drag/model.ts`: `resolveDrop` only calls `onClickTarget` on glow testids, which are targets, so dragging is unaffected.
- Any other file, crate, `spec/`, `BUILD.md`, `crates/cards/patches/` and the forbidden paths.

This is client input only, so there is no spec change and no new ruling. The governing rules are CLAUDE.md rule 7 and the existing R1200 (cited, already has a note) and R849000 (unchanged). No patch fragment is needed: web-only patches such as #1609 and #1770 added none.

## Steps

1. **`apps/web/src/game/actions.ts`, new helper.** Add this function directly after `startActivation` (which ends just before the `/** One click. …` doc comment of `onClickTarget`, around line 930). Copy it exactly:

   ```ts
   /**
    * Picks a unit up to attack with it: the attacks `legal` lists for it become the candidates.
    * R1200: while a Mayor acts the attack names no target, so the click sends it at once. `null` when
    * `legal` offers the unit no attack.
    */
   function startAttack(legal: readonly ActionBody[], attackerId: string): ClickResult | null {
     const candidates = attacksBy(legal, attackerId);
     if (candidates.length === 0) return null;
     const only = candidates.length === 1 ? candidates[0] : undefined;
     if (only?.targetId === RANDOM_ATTACK_TARGET) return { interaction: IDLE, action: only };
     return { interaction: { stage: "attacking", attackerId, candidates } };
   }
   ```

   `attacksBy`, `RANDOM_ATTACK_TARGET`, `IDLE`, `ClickResult` and `ActionBody` are already in scope in this file. Add no imports.

2. **`apps/web/src/game/actions.ts`, `onClickTarget`, attacking branch** (`case "unit": case "backrow":`, the `if (interaction.stage === "attacking") { … }` block, around lines 980–990). Keep the deselect line and the `const action = interaction.candidates…find(…)` lookup exactly as they are. Replace only the final line, `return action === undefined ? { interaction } : { interaction: IDLE, action };`, with:

   ```ts
           if (action !== undefined) return { interaction: IDLE, action };
           // The other attackers stay clickable (`highlightFor`), so a click on one switches the attack to
           // it, as dragging it does (`planAttack`); a target of the picked attacker is read first, above.
           return startAttack(legal, target.instanceId) ?? { interaction };
   ```

3. **`apps/web/src/game/actions.ts`, `onClickTarget`, idle path** (the code after the `isBuilding` block in the same case, around lines 1007–1017). Replace everything from `const candidates = attacksBy(legal, target.instanceId);` through `return { interaction: { stage: "attacking", attackerId: target.instanceId, candidates } };` with:

   ```ts
         const started = startAttack(legal, target.instanceId);
         if (started !== null) return started;
         // R849000: legal offers this unit no attack; say why in the engine's words where the view gives
         // them (`UnitView.attackReason`, on the viewer's own units only). Nothing is sent.
         const reason = view.you.units.find((unit) => unit?.instanceId === target.instanceId)?.attackReason;
         return reason === undefined ? { interaction } : { interaction, notice: reason };
   ```

   The idle behaviour is unchanged. The old `// R1200: …` comment and the `only` lines now live in `startAttack`, so delete them here. Leave the `"hero"` case untouched.

4. **`apps/web/src/game/actions.test.ts`.** Add the five tests below inside `describe("the attack flow", …)`, after `it("emits the switchPosition the engine listed", …)` and before that describe's closing `});`. Use the describe's own `const view = seatedView();`, where `u1` is your lane 1, `u2` your lane 2 and `e1` the opponent's lane 1. Write each click as `onClickTarget(view, legal, <interaction>, { on: "unit", instanceId: "<id>", side: "you", lane: <n> })`, following `it("deselects the attacker when it is clicked again", …)`.

## Tests

All five go in `apps/web/src/game/actions.test.ts`, `describe("the attack flow")`. Each first picks `u1` from `IDLE` (`const attacking = onClickTarget(view, legal, IDLE, <u1 click>).interaction;`) and then clicks again from `attacking`.

1. `it("switches the attack to another attacker when it is clicked", …)`
   - `legal = [{ type: "attack", attackerId: "u1", targetId: "e1" }, { type: "attack", attackerId: "u2", targetId: "e1" }, { type: "attack", attackerId: "u2", targetId: heroTargetId("p2") }]`.
   - Click `u2` (lane 2).
   - Expect `result.action` toBeUndefined.
   - Expect `result.interaction` toEqual `{ stage: "attacking", attackerId: "u2", candidates: [legal[1], legal[2]] }`.
2. `it("attacks a unit the picked attacker can target even when that unit can attack too", …)`
   - `legal = [{ type: "attack", attackerId: "u1", targetId: "u2" }, { type: "attack", attackerId: "u2", targetId: "e1" }]`.
   - Click `u2`.
   - Expect `result.action` toEqual `{ type: "attack", attackerId: "u1", targetId: "u2" }`.
   - Expect `result.interaction` toEqual `IDLE`.
3. `it("deselects the attacker when it is clicked again, with another attacker listed", …)`
   - `legal = [{ type: "attack", attackerId: "u1", targetId: "e1" }, { type: "attack", attackerId: "u2", targetId: "e1" }]`.
   - Click `u1` again.
   - Expect `result.action` toBeUndefined.
   - Expect `result.interaction` toEqual `IDLE`.
4. `it("ignores a click on a unit with no attack while an attack is in flight", …)`
   - `legal = [{ type: "attack", attackerId: "u1", targetId: "e1" }, { type: "switchPosition", instanceId: "u2" }]`.
   - Click `u2`.
   - Expect `result.action` toBeUndefined.
   - Expect `result.notice` toBeUndefined.
   - Expect `result.interaction` toBe `attacking` (the same object, as in "ignores an attack target no candidate names").
5. `it("sends a random attack at once when the attack is switched to it", …)`
   - `const random: ActionBody = { type: "attack", attackerId: "u2", targetId: RANDOM_ATTACK_TARGET };`
   - `legal = [{ type: "attack", attackerId: "u1", targetId: "e1" }, random]`.
   - Click `u2`.
   - Expect `result.action` toEqual `random`.
   - Expect `result.interaction` toEqual `IDLE`.

Test titles carry no R-ids. Without step 2, tests 1 and 5 fail. Test 2 pins that the target reading wins.

Commands, from the repository root:
- `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh`. Run it once first: without it vitest fails with "Failed to resolve import ./pkg/jackioh_wasm.js". On the base, after this build, `actions.test.ts` passes 67 tests.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/game/actions.test.ts`
- `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/test/ux/drag-model.test.ts src/test/ux/glow.test.ts src/test/ux/glow-render.test.tsx src/game/sick.test.tsx src/game/activate.test.ts`. These are regression checks: each of these files calls `onClickTarget`, so the refactor must keep them green.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/game/actions.ts apps/web/src/game/actions.test.ts`

## Done when

- [ ] With legal attacks for `u1` and `u2`, clicking `u1` then `u2` gives `{ stage: "attacking", attackerId: "u2", … }` and no action (test 1).
- [ ] A click on a legal target of the picked attacker still returns that attack, even when that target is itself an attacker (test 2).
- [ ] A click on the picked attacker still drops it (test 3 and the existing "deselects the attacker when it is clicked again").
- [ ] A click on a unit with no legal attack while attacking leaves the interaction unchanged (test 4).
- [ ] An R1200 random-target attack is sent on the switching click (test 5).
- [ ] Every command under **Tests** passes.
- [ ] The harness's web tests step passes. `cargo` checks and `spec check` should be unaffected (no Rust or spec change; R1200 is still cited and still has its note).
- [ ] `git status` shows only the two files above (`apps/web/src/wasm/pkg` is ignored).

## Risks

- **Precedence.** The target lookup has to run before `startAttack`, or a unit that is both a target and an attacker would switch instead of being attacked. Step 2 keeps that order, and test 2 pins it.
- **Idle behaviour drift.** The idle path must still give the R849000 notice and the R1200 instant send. `sick.test.tsx` and the existing "sends a random attack on the attacker's click" cover both, so run them.
- **Drag.** `resolveDrop` (`drag/model.ts:297`) passes only glow testids, which are the picked attacker's targets, to `onClickTarget`. The target lookup always matches those first, so drop behaviour does not change. `drag-model.test.ts` holds this.
- **Hidden information and replay.** Not affected: the change reads only `legal` and builds the same `ActionBody`s the engine listed.

## Open questions

None needs a person. Two decisions the issue left open:

- **No notice on a miss while attacking.** A click on your own unit with an `attackReason` but no attack, made during an attack, stays silent, as it is today. Criterion 4 asks for an unchanged interaction. I rejected showing the R849000 reason there.
- **Shared helper.** I extracted the idle path into `startAttack` rather than copying the R1200 check into the attacking branch. I rejected the copy because it would duplicate the rule.
````

- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/game/actions.ts apps/web/src/game/actions.test.ts`

## Done when

- [ ] With legal attacks for `u1` and `u2`, clicking `u1` then `u2` gives `{ stage: "attacking", attackerId: "u2", … }` and no action (test 1).
- [ ] A click on a legal target of the picked attacker still returns that attack, even when that target is itself an attacker (test 2).
- [ ] A click on the picked attacker still drops it (test 3 and the existing "deselects the attacker when it is clicked again").
- [ ] A click on a unit with no legal attack while attacking leaves the interaction unchanged (test 4).
- [ ] An R1200 random-target attack is sent on the switching click (test 5).
- [ ] Every command under **Tests** passes.
- [ ] The harness's web tests step passes. `cargo` checks and `spec check` should be unaffected (no Rust or spec change; R1200 is still cited and still has its note).
- [ ] `git status` shows only the two files above (`apps/web/src/wasm/pkg` is ignored).

## Risks

- **Precedence.** The target lookup has to run before `startAttack`, or a unit that is both a target and an attacker would switch instead of being attacked. Step 2 keeps that order, and test 2 pins it.
- **Idle behaviour drift.** The idle path must still give the R849000 notice and the R1200 instant send. `sick.test.tsx` and the existing "sends a random attack on the attacker's click" cover both, so run them.
- **Drag.** `resolveDrop` (`drag/model.ts:297`) passes only glow testids, which are the picked attacker's targets, to `onClickTarget`. The target lookup always matches those first, so drop behaviour does not change. `drag-model.test.ts` holds this.
- **Hidden information and replay.** Not affected: the change reads only `legal` and builds the same `ActionBody`s the engine listed.

## Open questions

None needs a person. Two decisions the issue left open:

- **No notice on a miss while attacking.** A click on your own unit with an `attackReason` but no attack, made during an attack, stays silent, as it is today. Criterion 4 asks for an unchanged interaction. I rejected showing the R849000 reason there.
- **Shared helper.** I extracted the idle path into `startAttack` rather than copying the R1200 check into the attacking branch. I rejected the copy because it would duplicate the rule.
